core_meaning.primary_meaning: Joseph is a masculine name from the Hebrew Yosef (יוֹסֵף), explained in Genesis as “he will add”: Rachel names her son saying, “The LORD shall add to me another son.” It is the name of Joseph son of Jacob in Genesis and of Saint Joseph of Nazareth, husband of Mary.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: He will add / may he add (Hebrew root y-s-p)
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Genesis gives two explanations: the word asaf, “taken away” (“God hath taken away my reproach”), and the root y-s-p, “add” (“The LORD shall add to me another son”). The Jewish Encyclopedia treats it as a theophoric name, written once in Psalms as Jehoseph.

etymology.morphology: Imperfect verb form of y-s-p, “to add”, used as a name.
etymology.etymology_explanation: From Hebrew Yosef; Genesis 30:23–24 plays on asaf (“taken away”) and y-s-p (“add”).

origin.origin_explanation: Biblical Hebrew; in the 1st century CE Yosef was the second most popular male name among Jews. The Qur'anic and Arabic form is Yūsuf.

religion.primary_association: Christian — Joseph of Genesis and Saint Joseph
religion.religious_explanation: In Genesis Joseph is Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. In the New Testament Joseph of Nazareth is the husband of Mary, mother of Jesus, and Joseph of Arimathea supplied the tomb in which Jesus was buried.

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: Giuseppe was the most common male name in 20th-century Italy; in Israel the name is often Yossi or Yossef.

name_variants.variant_notes: José (Spanish/Portuguese), Giuseppe (Italian), Josef (German/Czech), Yusuf/Yūsuf (Arabic, Turkish), Yossi (Israeli pet form); Joe and Joey are English short forms.

known_linguistic_history: Yosef was the second most popular male name for Jews in the 1st century CE.
Joseph stayed in the US top 10 boys' names from 1925 to 1972.
historical_context.historical_person_association: Joseph son of Jacob; Saint Joseph of Nazareth.

modern_usage.modern_context: Remained in the US top 10 boys' names from 1925 to 1972 (with Robert); common worldwide as José, Giuseppe, Josef and Yusuf.
